observations.notes: FY25 record revenue SAR 77.8bn (+2.5%), EBITDA SAR 24.5bn (+6.1% ex-one-offs), long-term loans SAR 14.4bn.

recovery_analysis.thesis: PIF sovereign telecom champion; rock-solid A+ balance sheet, negligible net debt, dominant Saudi market share.

annotations.note: 9M26 rev SAR 60.1bn, EBITDA SAR 19.2bn (31.9%), NPAT SAR 10.9bn, debt SAR 23.7bn, cash SAR 8.3bn.
Long-term master lease agreements (10-15 year tenors) with Tier-1 telecom operators featuring contractual annual inflation escalators and power cost pass-through.
Expanding tenancy ratio (1.6x - 2.1x) yields substantial operating leverage, driving rapid organic deleveraging with minimal incremental capex.
Contracted multi-year revenue backlog exceeding 6-8x annual revenues guarantees high earnings visibility and predictable debt service capacity.
9M26 rev SAR 60.10bn (+3.7%), op profit SAR 11.28bn (+4.1%), NI SAR 10.92bn, cash dividends SAR 8.2bn.

verdict.stance: Neutral / Ultra-Low Leverage IG Cash Cow (A1/A+) with Rising Dividends & Capex
verdict.summary: 9M26 revenue grew +3.7% YoY to SAR 60.10bn and operating profit rose +4.1% to SAR 11.28bn, though 9M net profit edged down to SAR 10.92bn (vs SAR 11.58bn 9M25) on higher net finance costs. Declared SAR 8.2bn 9M cash dividends while keeping ~0.65x ultra-conservative net leverage.

positives: Fortress balance sheet (~0.65x net leverage) and A1/A+ sovereign-linked Saudi IG ratings.
Stable core telecom cash generation: 9M26 operating profit +4.1% YoY to SAR 11.28bn.
Growth vectors in Tawal towers, stc Bank, and data centers/AI infrastructure.
negatives: Generous dividend policy (SAR 8.2bn in 9M26) plus international M&A (Telefónica stake / CEE towers) consumes cash.
Higher net financing costs trimmed 9M26 net income to SAR 10.92bn (vs SAR 11.58bn).
Tight IG credit spreads leave minimal RV cushion.
